notes.title: 23rd of September Update
notes.notes: [p]Hello![/p][p][/p][p]I've uploaded an update containing the following changes:[/p][list][*][p][b]Item comparison[/b] is now implemented. Colored + and - icons will show next to attributes like range, damage or ship stats like armor and shield when viewing both weapons and modules. These icons show whether a stat is better or worse than the existing, already installed item. On weapons, hovering over an installed weapon will switch the comparison so it is always relative to the selected weapon. Note that not all attributes are compared: Set bonuses, perks, burst behaviour and ability values are still as-is. This change was one of the longest-requested from way back during private testing - I expect it will help ease some players into the loot game by taking a part of the cognitive load of item comparison off their shoulders.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Forge buffs[/b] have been updated to be exclusively bonus-based instead of the prior trade-off behaviour. While most forge buffs were already strict improvements, the upgrades to weapons contained trade-offs that made them much less desirable than almost all other upgrades. I have decided to remove the negative components from these upgrades entirely so that all forge buffs are now improvements with no drawbacks. This will make the choice of which buff to pick more engaging and raise player power by a small amount overall.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Material and scrap costs for upgrades[/b] have been slightly tweaked to make the health-related upgrades more affordable. Shield, armor and hull point upgrades have had their scalars reduced, meaning the increase in their scrap cost per upgrade purchased is reduced. The armor point upgrade has had its exotic matter cost converted to plasteel cost - this change is intended to address the pre-armor-regen early game situation, where flat armor is nearly useless compared to regen and no real choice is possible because both upgrades cost rare and valuable exotic matter. While armor regen will remain a crucial stepping stone in the transition from early to midgame, players can now invest into flat armor to make incremental survivability gains before the "big jump".[/p][/*][/list][p]As always, please leave any feedback you have either in the discussion forums or on the discord, and I hope you have fun![/p]

notes.title: 12th of September Update
notes.notes: [p]Hello![/p][p][/p][p]I just pushed an update with the following changes:[/p][list][*][p]A [b]weapon and module selection menu[/b] has been added after embarkation. This menu allows players to pick a weapon type for the first slot as well as spend credits (250 per) to start with a module in each slot. In addition, playing the tutorial now guarantees that the first weapon is a laser. This change was made to address the frustration of bad starting weapon RNG, particularly when spawning with all launchers. It should allow some mitigation of this issue as well as build planning when used in concert with some of the pre-embark temporary bonuses. While weapon selection is free, modules have a small credit cost to offset the power boost from weapon selection and provide a credit sink.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Resolution options[/b] have been tweaked to properly show the current running resolution as well as be visually coherent with the rest of the UI. The resolution dropdown now offers resolutions based on your display instead of the previous hand-written list.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Small UI tweaks[/b] have been made to improve tutorial flow and make the cruise button more "buttony".[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]There's also a secret change that allows the secret achievement to be earned, but obviously I can't say much more about that![/p][p][/p][p]I hope you enjoy this update and feel that it makes your runs more consistent going forward.[/p]

notes.title: 7th of September Update: Photo Mode and New Achievements
notes.notes: [p]Hello![/p][p]I've pushed a new build that includes the following new features and changes:[/p][list][*][p][b]Photo Mode[/b] (returns)[b]:[/b] You can now enable a photo mode from the pause menu. In this mode you can move the camera freely using your controls for Pitch/Roll, Yaw, Throttle, View and Zoom. When activating photo mode, time stops and all UI elements are made invisible. Photo mode uses a traditional WASD+Mouselook setup for movement that may be awkward using custom keybinds, specific photo mode keybinds will come at a later date. Keep in mind that the modifier key used to rotate the camera in normal play is required to move the photo mode camera as well. The mode can be exited by using the respective pause menu option. Note that there is no built-in photo taking function, please use Steam's built-in screenshot option or other capture software. [b]Be aware:[/b] Photo Mode has a technical limitation that I haven't yet been able to fix - when entering photo mode without having the sun in your field of view, its lens flare effect will be missing inside of photo mode. Conversely, when entering photo mode while having the sun in your field of view, its lens flare will be duplicated on the other side of the skybox. This is something I hope to be able to fix before release but remains an issue right now, so I decided to ship photo mode regardless.[/p][/*][*][p][b]New Achievements:[/b] I've added two new achievements: [i]Navigator[/i] for those that defeat the demo's final boss, and [i]Shipwright[/i] for those who unlock all ships in the demo. These will unlock retroactively, so if you've already done these things just start up the game and they should pop up. Regardless of how you unlock them, you may need to exit Catharage to get the Steam notification.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Dreadnought buffs:[/b] The Dreadnought has received a fifth weapon slot as well as slight buffs to its speed and maneuverability. This is intended to help it stand out as a more viable option next to the battleship and mothership, both of which have clearly identifiable strengths that the dreadnought has struggled to match. I'm collecting feedback on the ship-ship balancing and will tweak it further as release nears, so make sure to let me know what you think about your favourite (or least favourite) ships![/p][/*][/list][p]I hope you have fun with photo mode and can get some cool shots, and maybe chase one of the new achievements![/p]

notes.title: End of August Update
notes.notes: [p]Hey everyone![/p][p][/p][p]I just pushed an update containing a number of QOL and polish features:[/p][p][/p][list][*][p][b]Free floating scrap and credit chests[/b] now track to the player like materials do.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Scrapping loot[/b] now shows a preview of the potential scrap value gained. This value is now influenced by rarity, and most items are worth more. This should make it easier to gain scrap throughout normal play rather than just in large bursts when collecting Keystones.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Suspending [/b]now correctly stores and restores individual drone slots, meaning the [i]Odachi[/i] hybrid battleship and runs with at least 2 [i]Summoner[/i] set bonus points can be suspended without losing drone slots.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Targeting Overlay layering[/b] has been improved. Target Icons remain layered behind normal UI elements as they currently are but selecting them will move the expanded detail view in front of all other UI, making it no longer obstructed by things like weapon slots or the radial targeting menu.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Throttle and Agility UI[/b] has been altered to be bar-based instead of text-based. A two-bar display now sits where the Throttle Text used to be, reducing the reliance on numbers. Throttle and agility behaviour is unchanged.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Small UI tweaks[/b] include a unit display for weapons to show which unit fire delay is measured in (ticks for lasers, seconds for launchers/guns). In addition, the [b]reset[/b] button has been moved from the pause menu to the main menu, distanced from other buttons and has had a confirmation window added to prevent accidental save game deletion. Module slots now show even if the module has no ability or set bonus.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]I also want to touch one some changes that are currently work-in-progress but will arrive before launch (and ideally quite soon):[/p][p]-comparison mode between new and old items is proving more complicated than anticipated and will be coming in a future update[/p][p]-individual axis steering adjustments for outlier ships like the [i]Destroyer[/i] is incoming, but not finalized as this is a very "deep" change that touches many systems[/p][p]-a "reverse" throttle mode is potentially coming, depending on whether I can figure out how to make it work with trails properly - there's some work that needs to be done with trails as is[/p][p]-cruise particle issues persist with certain ships, and this is an issue that I currently cannot reproduce so it remains difficult to solve[/p][p][/p][p]That's all for today, I hope you enjoy the new update![/p]

notes.title: Devlog: Starmap, Progression and Faction Objectives
notes.notes: [p]Hello![/p][p][/p][p]In this first devlog-style post I want to lay out the structure of the release version in more detail, going over how warping, objectives and unlocks will work as well as expanding on the "sectors" concept I mentioned in the demo announcement.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45702476/9afbc9c018dc9d0a22534e6e29eaa024987f42d0.png"][/img][/p][p][b]The Starmap[/b][/p][p][/p][p]I'm currently working on the starmap, a central part of the release content system. This interface will appear when the "Warp" button is pressed, replacing the fully random warp with a player selection. On the map, a persistent, infinite grid of cells represents space, with colors denoting the dominant faction in the area. The central cell is the player's current location. Several cells will be highlighted (as shown above) - these are potential warp candidates. Players can hover over them to see the dominant faction in that area as well as a listing of neighboring faction influence. Clicking will initiate a warp to this new location. A cell's dominant faction as well as surrounding influence determine what types of POIs and enemies can spawn there. For example, an area with Sentinel control and Catharingian influence may spawn a Sentinel Fortress as its main POI, with a Catharingian Outpost as a minor location. Since faction POIs also hold the required objects, ships and mechanics for faction objectives, targeting specific regions of space enables players to control their game's pace and difficulty.[/p][p][/p][p]Concerning difficulty, the starmap will also incorporate an existing feature: Warping while on cooldown. In the demo, Warping incurs a cooldown displayed in red on the Warp button. It is still possible to Warp while this cooldown is active, but doing so will increase the difficulty of the next encounter by double the normal amount. So far, this was conceptualized both as a "skip" for strong players to reach hard content sooner as well as a punishment for using Warp as a way out of hard situations. In the new System, these functions will remain, but warping while on cooldown will enable players to jump longer distances on the starmap, making it possible to use this feature as a movement tool.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45702476/4a889e9304b9627482cc9d6ed468eb62f9661602.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Faction Objectives and Unlocks[/b][/p][p][/p][p]Different factions and free movement would be meaningless without a reason to go places, and this is where the new faction objectives will come in. In the demo, there is one set of objectives, that being the hunt for Keystones and the confrontation with the Scipio. These will become the Sentinel (blue faction) objectives on release, and new objectives in the same style will be added for all of the other four factions. On the new Objectives Screen the status of these tasks can be viewed. Like in the demo, completing individual tasks that are part of faction objectives will enable new POIs and enemies to spawn in the corresponding areas. Unlocks are similarly gated, such that progressing through each faction's objectives will enable the purchase of new ships and new permanent meta upgrades. Factions are somewhat themed, so players can focus on one to strengthen a specific playstyle. For example, finishing the Verdant Swarm objective chain unlocks the ability to permanently upgrade the starting armor of all drones - a very powerful tool for aspiring carrier pilots.[/p][p][/p][p]My aim is that this structure provides an understandable, approachable set of goals that players can attain on their own terms. Like many aspects of Catharage, the "extraction" spirit of player-driven agency and risk management plays a big role in the Starmap and Faction Objectives. While this is work-in-progress and subject to change, I hope I've given you an idea of what the final game will be like. As always, please leave feedback on the discussion forums or the discord![/p]

notes.title: Unified Camera Mode, Launcher Buffs and Tutorial Tweaks
notes.notes: [p]Hello![/p][p]I've updated the demo to address camera handling, launcher performance and the tutorial:[/p][p][/p][list][*][p][b]Unified Camera Modes[/b]: Instead of the previous distinction between "normal" operation and the "fighter mode", the camera now has two separate modes of operation: [b]Ship-aligned[/b] (the new default) and [b]horizon-aligned[/b] (the old default). In ship-aligned mode, the camera rotation follows the player ship, and as a result, steering inputs are relative to the camera. In horizon-aligned mode, camera rotation is independent from the ship's rotation. The key previously used to switch to fighter cam (standard bind C) can now be used to toggle between these modes. Unlike before, Overview is available in ship-aligned mode and will similarly rotate with the ship. This mode preference is persistent across sessions. To account for these changes, the tutorial will no longer swap between reference frames and remain entirely in ship-aligned mode unless players choose to change modes.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Missile Launcher Buff[/b]: Missile launchers have occupied a weird niche in the combat sandbox of Catharage, being significantly less effective against most targets than both cannons and lasers, and being insufficiently specialized to fill their own role in a clear and understandable manner. While launchers already had a higher range stat than other weapons, this did not make up for their comparative lack of utility. I've [b]increased both the base damage and the scaling damage[/b] components of the missile launcher loot equation, meaning launchers will now start with higher damage numbers and gain more damage as difficulty increases compared to lasers and cannons. This should help them solidify a role as hard-hitting long range options against larger targets.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Tutorial Tweaks[/b]: In addition to the camera-related change detailed above, the tutorial has been adjusted to show less information early on. To avoid overloading and distracting players, several UI elements are disabled until certain milestones in the tutorial flow are reached. The training drones that usually loiter in the staging area have been disabled as well.[/p][/*][*][p][b]UI Layering Tweak[/b]: The sensor contact display has been moved to a UI layer behind the rest of the interface. Previously, opening loot, displaying tutorial messages and the general interactive HUD were overlapped by targeting icons, which lead to text readability issues and could even disrupt the timestop behaviour of several windows. Sensor contacts have now been moved to a lower UI layer, meaning all standard UI elements draw above them. While this is a temporary solution that presents its own issues, it should alleviate text problems especially during the tutorial and item handling. I will work to develop a more sophisticated system for handling UI layering for the final release.[/p][/*][/list][p]I hope you like these changes! As always, please leave any feedback you have on the steam discussion forums or the discord, and go shoot some missiles![/p]

notes.title: Demo Update: New Suspend Feature, Camera Controls & More
notes.notes: [p]Hey everyone,[/p][p][/p][p]I just pushed a major update to the demo, based on player feedback and outstanding fixes and goals:[/p][p][/p][list][*][p][b]Suspend Feature: [/b]I've added a new option to the pause menu called "[b]suspend & quit[/b]" that allows you to save elements of your current run to resume later. This button will save your [b]current ship, all equipment[/b] (weapons & modules) [b]and its stats[/b] including set bonuses. Your collected [b]currency is also saved[/b] and restored. Fleet members you have recruited will not rejoin you. The suspend option is available from your first warp onward. If a suspended state is available, the "embark" option in the main menu will be replaced with a "suspend" option that will spawn you in the training area with your recovered ship, currency and items. While I've tested this system and already fixed a whole heap of new and exotic errors that came with it, some edge cases may still exist where stats or items are not saved and restored correctly. If you come across these, please report to me (with details) so I can investigate.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][list][*][p][b]Fighter Cam Orbit Rotation:[/b] The "Fighter Cam" now allows for camera orbit rotation just like the main game cam. Press your camera orbit key (default Right Mouse Button) and move the mouse to rotate this view. These new controls respect the inversion and sensitivity settings in the options menu just like the main camera rotation does.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][list][*][p]Persistence for Button Guide toggle: The game now saves the state of the Button Guide menu, meaning you don't have to toggle it every time you start.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]I hope you enjoy these new features and get some long runs going, and if you've struggled with the movement and camera before, maybe the new controls can help you![/p]

notes.title: Demo Bugfixes and QOL Update
notes.notes: [p]I've just uploaded a small demo update addressing some outstanding bugs and implementing feedback.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Changelog[/b][/p][list][*][p]fixed a bug where fleet members would show up on the targeting display despite being dead[/p][/*][*][p]camera switching is now possible from all states to all other states[/p][/*][*][p]sensor contact health display has been made independent from cursor hover state and can be viewed without hovering, as long as sensor solution is strong enough. If you have feedback or suggestions, please post them either on the Steam discussion board or the game's Discord.[/p]

notes.title: Free Demo Out Now!
notes.notes: [p][b]Hello everyone![/b][/p][p]I am very happy to announce that the public [b]steam demo is now available for download![/b][/p][p]If you are interested in Catharage, make sure you check it out and give your feedback. The demo represents an in-development state of the game that is not final, and all aspects are subject to change. To expand on the usual fare with these statements a bit:[/p][p][b]Content[/b] - The demo includes the first "Sector" of content (a concept I detail below), which should last anywhere from 3-5 hours depending on your knowledge, skill and luck. I do not currently plan to update the demo with more new content.[/p][p][b]Stability[/b] - The demo build is stable and relatively bug-free. My testing capacity is limited so it's likely that there are bugs and issues that have slipped through the cracks, so please let me know in the discussion forums or on the discord if you find any![/p][p][b]Performance[/b] - Catharage uses global raymarched volumetrics for its lighting. This is a feature that cannot be turned off, as it is critical for the look of the game. These volumetrics are demanding to render, so the game may run worse than you expect given its stylized look. Performance can be improved by using the "Volumetrics Downsampling" option in the graphics menu. I will also work on performance for the release version and you can expect that version to perform better than the demo.[/p][p][/p][p]Catharage is a complex and dense game. It is [b]highly recommended to play the Tutorial[/b] before doing anything else, as it will familiarize you with core concepts that you need to survive in the game.[/p][p]Note also that it is currently not possible to "save" a run in progress, and it is also impossible to end a run without either extracting, dying or quitting the game.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][b]Roadmap and future of the game[/b][/p][p][/p][p]I plan to release the full game in winter, likely around christmas. Until then I will continue to fix and refine core gameplay and develop new content. As mentioned above, the demo features one "Sector" of content. A sector is comprised of POIs, Ships, Upgrades, Weapon Perks, Abilities and Enemies as well as an overarching objective to complete. Since only one sector is currently in the demo, all these elements are available at the same time and in the same place. For the full release I plan to include 3 or 4 of these sectors and distribute them in a spatial, player-controlled way. I'm not sure yet how exactly this will look, likely something akin to a starmap, but it means that in the full version, you'll be able to choose what distribution of content your encounter and upgrade sheet will feature, and you'll be able to progress through different content sectors at your own pace. This structure will also enable me to release future post-release content packs seamlessly into the game. Depending on the response to the game it may end up being updated for a good while to come.[/p][p][/p][p]With that all said, have fun with the demo, kill some ships and make sure to let me know what you think![/p][p][/p][p]Björn Michalski[/p]
